name_en: Best approximation problem in a Euclidean space
name_zh: 欧几里得空间中的最佳逼近问题
statement: Given a Euclidean space V, a finite-dimensional subspace S, and an element x in V, determine the element of S whose distance from x is as small as possible. Section 15.14 sets up this problem, illustrates it by a plane in V_3, and announces that the projection of x on S is its solution.

anchors.quote: We wish to consider the following type of approximation problem: Given an element x in V, to determine an element in S whose distance from x is as small as possible.
We prove next that the projection of $x$ on $S$ is the solution to the approximation problem stated at the beginning of this section.

name_en: Distance between two elements of a Euclidean space
name_zh: 欧几里得空间中两元素间的距离
statement: The distance between two elements x and y is defined to be the norm ||x - y||. This turns the norm of 15.10 into the quantity minimized in the approximation problem.

anchors.quote: The distance between two elements x and y is defined to be the norm $\|x - y\|$

statement: An element of a Euclidean space V is said to be orthogonal to a subset S of V if it is orthogonal to every element of S. This lifts orthogonality between two elements (15.11) to orthogonality between an element and an entire set.

anchors.quote: An element in V is said to be orthogonal to S if it is orthogonal to every element of S.
Let S be a subset of a Euclidean space V.

name_en: Notation S perp for the set of all elements orthogonal to S
name_zh: 记号 S 垂直(与 S 正交的全体元素)
statement: The set of all elements orthogonal to a subset S is denoted by S with a perpendicular superscript and is read 'S perpendicular'. The same symbol is used for the orthogonal complement when S is a subspace.

statement: When S is a subspace of a Euclidean space V, the subspace S perp of all elements orthogonal to S is called the orthogonal complement of S. Geometrically, the orthogonal complement of a plane through the origin in V_3 is the line through the origin perpendicular to it.

anchors.quote: In case S is a subspace, then $S^{\perp}$ is called the orthogonal complement of S.
If S is a plane through the origin, as shown in Figure 15.2, then $S^{\perp}$ is a line through the origin perpendicular to this plane.

name_en: S perp is a subspace whether or not S is one
name_zh: S 垂直总是子空间(无论 S 本身是否为子空间)
statement: For any subset S of a Euclidean space V, the set of all elements orthogonal to S is a subspace of V, even when S itself is not a subspace. Apostol states this and leaves the verification as a simple exercise.

anchors.quote: It is a simple exercise to verify that $S^{\perp}$ is a subspace of V, whether or not S itself is one.

name_en: Orthogonal decomposition of an element relative to a subspace
name_zh: 元素相对于子空间的正交分解
statement: A representation of an element x as a sum x = s + s perp with s in the subspace S and s perp in S perp. Theorem 15.15 asserts that such a decomposition exists and is unique whenever S is finite-dimensional.

anchors.quote: First we prove that an orthogonal decomposition (15.16) actually exists.
Next we prove that the orthogonal decomposition (15.16) is unique.

statement: Let V be a Euclidean space and S a finite-dimensional subspace. Then every x in V can be written uniquely as x = s + s perp with s in S and s perp in S perp, and the norm of x obeys the Pythagorean formula. Existence is proved by taking a finite orthonormal basis of S and setting s equal to the sum of the projections of x along the basis elements; uniqueness follows because the zero element is the only element orthogonal to itself.

anchors.quote: THEOREM 15.15. ORTHOGONAL DECOMPOSITION THEOREM. Let V be a Euclidean space and let S be a finite-dimensional subspace of V.
Then every element x in V can be represented uniquely as a sum of two elements, one in S and one in $S^{\perp}$

name_en: Pythagorean formula for an orthogonal decomposition
statement: Part of Theorem 15.15: if x = s + s perp is the orthogonal decomposition of x relative to a finite-dimensional subspace S, then the square of the norm of x equals the sum of the squares of the norms of s and s perp, because the cross terms in the expansion of (s + s perp, s + s perp) vanish by orthogonality.

anchors.quote: Moreover, the norm of $x$ is given by the Pythagorean formula
the remaining terms being zero since $s$ and $s^{\perp}$ are orthogonal. This proves (15.17).

name_en: Projection of an element on a subspace
name_zh: 元素在子空间上的投影
statement: If {e_1, ..., e_n} is an orthonormal basis for a finite-dimensional subspace S of a Euclidean space V and x is in V, the element s given by the sum of (x, e_i) e_i is called the projection of x on the subspace S. It is exactly the S-component of the orthogonal decomposition of x, and Theorem 15.16 (in Section 15.15) shows it solves the approximation problem.

anchors.quote: is called the projection of $x$ on the subspace $S$
